page.title: AI strategy consulting for growing businesses.
page.lede: We map where your hours and money go, then hand you a ranked plan: what to automate now, what can wait, and what to leave alone.

forWho.title: Who it is for
forWho.intro: Leadership teams who know AI matters but do not want to spend on tools before they know where they fit.
signs: Your team uses AI here and there, but there is no plan behind it.
You have tried a pilot or two, and nothing has spread across the company.
You are being pitched AI software every week and cannot tell what is worth buying.
You want a clear first project, with the hours it should save, before you commit budget.

items.name: A time and workflow audit
items.body: How the work actually moves through your company, team by team, and where the hours go each week.

items.name: Ranked opportunities
items.body: Each one with an estimate of hours saved, cost to build and difficulty, sorted into automate now, wait, or leave alone.

items.name: A roadmap you can act on
items.body: The order to do things in, what each step needs, and who on your team owns it.

items.name: A first project, chosen together
items.body: We walk your leadership team through the plan and agree where to start.

steps.title: Kickoff
steps.body: One hour with you on your goals, where the business feels stuck, and what you have already tried.

steps.title: Interview
steps.body: Short one-on-ones with the people doing the work, so we see how each job moves from start to finish.

steps.title: Map
steps.body: We add up the hours each workflow takes every week and what that time costs you.

steps.title: Rank
steps.body: Each opportunity gets an estimate of hours saved, cost to build and difficulty, sorted into automate now, wait, or leave alone.

steps.title: Decide
steps.body: We walk your leadership team through the plan and choose the first project together.

examples.title: What it looks like in practice
examples.intro: A strategy engagement usually turns up a handful of quick wins and one or two bigger projects. A few recent examples:

items.body: Six ranked findings, including no system to flag clients who had gone quiet, and a four-day quick-wins plan the owner can run alone. Projected: about 9 hours a week back.
Four quick-win workflows, and a task that now prepares her for every meeting booked through her scheduling link. Projected: about 5.5 hours a week back.
The assessment found every new inquiry waited on a confidentiality agreement sent by hand. We then automated it on their own Gmail, HubSpot and PandaDoc.

faq.q: Do we need to be using AI already?
faq.a: No. Many companies start here before they have bought anything, so the plan decides which tools are worth paying for.

faq.q: Who from our team needs to be involved?
faq.a: One hour with you at the start, short one-on-ones with the people doing the work, and your leadership team for the final walkthrough.
Some teams run the quick wins themselves. Others have us build the first project, train the team, or stay on as a fractional chief AI officer to lead the rollout.

faq.q: Is this only for large companies?
faq.a: No. We work with growing businesses, from owner-led teams to companies with several departments. The plan is sized to how your business actually runs.
